subject: Week 1: The beginning, and the oldest questions
body:
Good morning.

Welcome to week one. This plan reads the Bible in the order it happened, so you start with creation, then jump straight into Job, likely the oldest story in the book, before returning to Abraham.

The oldest questions show up immediately: who is God, and can I trust Him when everything breaks? Do not solve Job. Just listen to him.

Heather

subject: Week 2: Out of Egypt, up the mountain
body:
Good morning.

The exodus this week: plagues, Passover, the Red Sea, Sinai, and the tabernacle, then into the wilderness with Numbers. God rescues His people first, then teaches them how to live. That order matters.

Thirteen chapters a day, about forty-five minutes. If you miss a day, just pick up with today. No guilt here.

Heather

subject: Week 3: Into the land
body:
Good morning.

Moses hands it off, Joshua crosses over, the judges spiral downward, and Ruth quietly refuses to leave. You end the week at the door of 1 Samuel.

Watch the pattern all week: forgetting God always costs, and crying out to Him always finds Him listening.

Heather

subject: Week 4: David, and the songs he lived
body:
Good morning.

Here is where this plan shines. David is anointed, runs for his life, and becomes king, and you read the psalms he wrote inside those exact moments. The caves produced the songs.

You will also start seeing the same stories told twice, from Samuel and from Chronicles. Two witnesses, one king.

Heather

subject: Week 5: A kingdom at its peak
body:
Good morning.

More psalms this week, David's hardest chapters, and then Solomon: the temple filled with glory, and wisdom poured into Proverbs.

The Bible does not hide what David did or what it cost. It just keeps showing a man who came back to God every time. That is the whole lesson.

Heather

subject: Week 6: Wisdom, and the tear
body:
Good morning.

Proverbs finishes, Ecclesiastes tells the truth, Song of Solomon sings, and then the kingdom splits in two. From here the story runs on two tracks, Israel and Judah, and you will read Kings and Chronicles side by side, the same kings from two angles.

Nobody drifts toward God. Watch how drift works this week.

Heather

subject: Week 7: The prophets arrive
body:
Good morning.

Now the prophets land exactly where they belong. Joel, Jonah, Amos, and Hosea preach to the very kings you are reading about. Elisha works quiet miracles while the throne rooms rot.

Hosea marries a woman who keeps leaving, because God wanted His people to feel how relentless His love is. Isaiah begins, and everything lifts.

Heather

subject: Week 8: Isaiah, Hezekiah, and the last warnings
body:
Good morning.

Isaiah 53 is this week. Read it slowly: pierced for our transgressions, written seven hundred years before the cross. Hezekiah prays a city back from the brink, Josiah finds the lost Book, and Jeremiah starts saying what nobody wants to hear.

The fall is coming, and the prophets knew. Their hope was never in the kingdom anyway.

Heather

subject: Week 9: The fall, and songs in a strange land
body:
Good morning.

Jerusalem burns this week. Jeremiah weeps through Lamentations, and Ezekiel sees the glory leave the temple and promises it will return.

Buried in the ashes is Jeremiah 31: a new covenant, written on hearts. That promise is why you are holding a Bible right now.

Heather

subject: Week 10: Exile faith, and the road home
body:
Good morning.

Ezekiel's dry bones stand up, Daniel keeps his window open toward Jerusalem, Esther steps up for such a time as this, and the first exiles head home to rebuild.

God's name never appears in Esther. His fingerprints are on every page. Same is true of plenty of seasons in our lives.

Heather

subject: Week 11: The last word, the silence, and the arrival
body:
Good morning.

Nehemiah rebuilds the wall, Malachi gets the Old Testament's last word, the psalter closes in praise, and then, after four hundred silent years, He arrives. You will be in the gospels by midweek.

Reading it in order, you will feel it: every promise you have read for ten weeks walks into the room.

Heather

subject: Week 12: One story, four witnesses, then fire
body:
Good morning.

The gospels finish and the Spirit falls. The church explodes through Acts, and the letters arrive in the order the churches got them: James first, then Galatians, Thessalonians, Corinthians, Romans.

These letters were written to real messes. That is why they still fit ours.

Heather

subject: Week 13: Hold fast. He makes all things new.
body:
Good morning.

The final week: Paul's last letters, Hebrews telling you to hold fast, Peter and John writing to scattered believers, and then Revelation. No more tears. No more death. All things new.

You read the whole Bible in ninety days, in the order it happened. I am so proud of you. Finish strong, then go get your certificate.

Heather
